Let's examine 3 fundamental strategies for real-world Information Science [[181]]; in essence, this would apply from virtually anything "knowledge-work" related, from websites to libraries, and even the construction of knowledge-sensitive fields. These knowledge-sensitive-driven fields include as stastics and especially the computational fields; where knowledge becomes executable by machines, which naturally explodes combinatorial space once a threshold of power is reached. This "entropic decay" demands proper systems-and-teams-communication; which is another form of knowledge and information exchange. Everything from the mollecular to the virtual; may inherit from these (proposed) abstractions [[106]].

The 3 proposed strategies include: 1. Topical, Collapsed, Graph-driven 1. Hierarchical, Inheritance, Abstraction 3. Systemata, Automata, Automation

Note that these models of definitely subject to change, and are based almost exclusively on personal Phenemonological experience working with highly complex knowledge systems.

Unravelling the first model; this is most commonly seen in Zettelkasten. The Human Brain also processes information, and decision, by the topical-collapsed-graph architecture. Powerful and scaleable as it may be, this structure comes with serious risks. These risks include incompleteness & combinatorial noise, where information is often "noise" before settling into fidelity. "Association-based-dependency" where information is not stored based on logical-topical-cluster-locale; but by it's associations and relations; often leading to "memory leaks" so-to-speak.
